variable_description: Total capital gains for the year worked out using the discount method, before any losses or concessions are applied. The ATO says a taxpayer uses one of three methods for each asset - "indexation method", "discount method, or" the "'other' method" - and the discount method is available only where the asset was held at least twelve months: "If you bought and sold your asset within 12 months, you must use the 'other' method". The split matters because the discount is not applied yet: "If you use the discount method, do not apply the discount percentage until you have applied current year capital losses and unapplied net capital losses from earlier years."
value_definition: A dollar amount, gross of losses, the CGT discount and the small business concessions. It pairs with the other-method total on the same row; adding the two gives total current year capital gains before any reduction.
limitation: The amount is a gross gain, not taxable income, and is several steps away from the net capital gain that reaches the return. A zero here does not mean no gains: it can mean every gain was worked out under the other or indexation method instead.
rationale: The DIL label names the total current year capital gains under the discount method, which is a defined step of the ATO capital gains tax schedule. The ATO guide defines the three methods, when each applies and where the discount is applied in the sequence.
evidence_quote: If you use the discount method, do not apply the discount percentage until you have applied current year capital losses and unapplied net capital losses from earlier years.

value_domain: Small business retirement exemption, discount method (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: The small business retirement exemption claimed against gains worked out under the discount method. The ATO describes it as follows: "The small business retirement exemption: this allows you to disregard capital gains for active assets (up to a lifetime limit of $500,000) if the conditions are satisfied." value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: Capital gains on collectables held for at least twelve months, reported by the entity under non-active assets. The ATO treats collectables as a separate class - "those relating to collectables (for example, jewellery)" - because their losses are ring-fenced: "You can only use capital losses from collectables to reduce capital gains from collectables." On a business file a non-zero value is unusual and generally marks an art or antique holding rather than trading stock. OF and NF in the DIL label are the old-form and new-form wordings.
value_definition: A dollar amount of gain on collectables, before the discount percentage is applied.
limitation: The ring-fencing means a loss on collectables cannot reduce any other gain. Assets held as trading stock are not collectables and belong elsewhere. The OF and NF reading is inferred.

value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax
variable_description: Capital gains on collectables not worked out under the discount method, which for a collectable usually means it was bought and sold within twelve months. The ATO ring-fences this class: "You can only use capital losses from collectables to reduce capital gains from collectables." It sits under non-active assets because a collectable cannot qualify for the small business concessions.
value_definition: A dollar amount of gain on collectables, with no discount applied.
limitation: The ring-fencing means a loss on collectables cannot reduce any other gain. Collectables below the acquisition threshold are disregarded entirely and never appear.
rationale: The DIL label names collectables capital gains for other capital gains within non-active assets, a defined part of the ATO capital gains tax schedule.
